'''Teeno''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Sith acolyte/Legends|Sith Acolyte]] who attended the [[Sith Academy (Korriban)|Sith Academy]] on [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] during the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]].<ref name="TOR" />

==Biography==
Along with fellow acolyte [[Phyne]], they held a hostility toward [[Vemrin]] who was very strong in the dark side. As a [[Empire's Wrath|promising Sith Warrior]] was about to meet [[Darth Baras]], Teeno, Phyne, and two other acolytes stood in stood in the antechamber to greet the acolyte. Knowing that Vemrin was going to have the new acolyte killed, they offered their assistance to eliminate Vemrin for the [[Sith Warrior]], so that they would not be punished for disobeying the rules.<ref name="TOR" />
{{GameDS}}
The Sith Warrior would consider their help, hinting that he agreed with their proposal. They obviously failed, since Vemrin returned from his trials. He then gloated how he murdered all the acolytes sent after him. Later, the warrior was contacted by a surviving Phyne, telling them how Teeno had been instantly killed by Vemrin and she was left crippled for many months. She realized Teeno was weak, her survival making her stronger than him.<ref name="TOR" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
Teeno is a non-playable character from the massively multi-player online role playing game ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' released by [[BioWare]] in [[2011]]. He is voiced by [[Fred Tatasciore]].<ref name="TOR" />

If the Warrior wasn't interested and refused their help, Teeno and Phyne offered to prove their skills to him/her in a duel, showing they were more than qualified to defeat and eliminate Vemrin. When the Sith Warrior agreed, Teeno, Phyne and the acolytes engaged him/her in a duel, in which they all lost. After their defeat, they realized they couldn't defeat Vemrin since the Sith Warrior was much stronger. Later, Phyne would contact the warrior, after witnessing Vemrin defeating six other acolytes and feeding their corpses to a tuk'ata. She thanked them for their survival and showing them the limits of their strength.<ref name="TOR" />
